output.summary: Approved G1032 design revision 2 (skill and docs only, no engine change; integrate and merge never read branch protection): when rulesets/rules/protection reads return 403, bootstrap from step 2 asks the owner for required check names (or proposes them from recent PR check runs) and records them in verification.required_ci before validate and landing; step 7 skips the rules probes and uses the repo endpoint; a declined CI gate is recorded in the bootstrap commit or PR message, and the owner is told an empty required_ci means no CI gate. docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md and INITIALIZATION.md gain the fallback. A guard test fails on any rules/rulesets/protection api call. Review approved after one round; implementer: update the Outcome and Finding sections to mention step 2.

responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: the fallback now starts at step 2 (required_ci is set from the owner or recent PR check runs before step 3 validates and step 4 lands); step 7 skips the rules probes; docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md line 12 is named.
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: risk text now says a misspelled name ends in 'required checks pending too long' after ci_timeout_minutes ('no checks appeared' fires only on an empty rollup); a declined gate is recorded in the bootstrap commit/PR message since POLICY has no field, and the guard test now fails on any rules/rulesets/protection api call.

output.summary: The engine never reads rulesets or protection, so this stays a skill and docs fix. The 403 fallback now sits in bootstrap step 2, where required_ci is first read, so it is set before validation and landing; step 7 and docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md line 12 point to it. Risk text corrected, a declined CI gate is recorded in the bootstrap commit or PR message, and the guard test fails on any rules, rulesets or protection api call.

Bootstrap SKILL.md step 2 gets the 403 fallback (owner or recent check names, set before validation, never silently empty, declined gate recorded); step 7 points back and runs repo-endpoint checks only; BRANCH_PROTECTION and INITIALIZATION get the pointer/section; HISTORY section 4 row added.

findings.text: Step 2 of SKILL.md also depends on the unreadable endpoint: 'required_ci (only always-running required check names, read once with `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/<I>`)'. It runs before step 7, so on a free-plan private repo the 403 hits there first, and the design only changes step 7 (and writes required_ci in the fallback, after POLICY was already written in step 2 and validated in step 3). Fix: have the design change step 2 as well: say that when that read returns 403 (or no rules), required_ci is filled from the owner/check-run fallback, and move or cross-reference the fallback so required_ci is set before step 3 validates and step 4 lands the files. Also name docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md line 12 (the rules/branches probe) among the edited places, and say the probe in step 7 and that doc is skipped on 403.

Risk text is wrong about the engine: 'A wrong check name makes integrate wait until the existing "no checks appeared" block'. That block fires only when the rollup is empty (`not rollup`). With other checks present and a misspelled required name, integrate stays pending and blocks with 'required checks pending too long' after verification.ci_timeout_minutes, with the same fix-required_ci option. Fix: describe both outcomes, and say a wrong name never silently passes (the name stays pending) while an empty list does. Also say where a declined gate is recorded (POLICY has no field for it; for example the intent text or the PR body), since 'record that merges then have no CI gate' has no named location.

output.summary: Both findings resolved. 1:1: the fallback now starts at SKILL.md step 2, so required_ci is set before step 3 validates and step 4 lands; step 7 skips the rules probes and docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md line 12 is named. 1:2: the risk text now matches the engine (misspelled name with other checks present gives 'required checks pending too long' after ci_timeout_minutes; 'no checks appeared' only on an empty rollup), a declined CI gate is recorded in the bootstrap commit or PR message, and the guard test fails on any rules/rulesets/protection api call. Non-blocking: the Outcome and Finding sections still say step 7 only, update them when implementing.

Tests match the approved design (rev with the step-2 fallback). At 52bce92: the 5 skill/doc tests in test_bootstrap_rules_unreadable fail on the current SKILL.md and docs (no 403, no --match-head-commit, no 'When rules are unreadable'), and the 3 engine tests pass by design. The fake-gh guard is effective: I injected a swallowed `gh api .../rules/branches/dev` call into ops/merge.py and test_integrate_and_merge_complete_without_reading_rules failed with the recorded call, so a future coupling is detected even if the engine tolerates the 403. The failing-check case still blocks. Non-blocking: several skill assertions are weak (owner, required_ci and zzzops/goal/** already occur in the current steps; 'match' is loose), the rules path regex does not see a rulesets query inside `gh api graphql`, and the design's 'if the repo read is also 403, ask the owner to confirm in the UI' is untested.

spec:
Found while designing G1003 (2026-11-01). Bootstrap step 7 assumes `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/<I>` and ruleset reads work, but a private repository on GitHub's free plan returns 403 for both. The skill gives no path for that case, so required_ci and merge settings cannot be read or set.

Give the skill (and validate's environment checks) a documented fallback: detect 403, explain that branch protection is unavailable on the plan, ask the owner for the required check names (or read them from recent PR check runs), record them in POLICY, and note that merges are then guarded by the engine's own CI gate only.

Acceptance: the skill documents the fallback; if validate or integrate change, engine tests cover the 403 path; docs/design edits per G1017's rule.
title: Bootstrap works when rulesets and branch protection are unreadable
